    tsdst.mcmc.msvec¶

    tsdst.mcmc.msvec(chain, b, method='bartlett')[source]¶

    Estimate the spectral covariance matrix of a centered MCMC chain.

    Translated from the lag-window estimator in R’s mcmcse package. Spectral covariance includes serial dependence across iterations. It is the asymptotic covariance of sqrt(n) times the Monte Carlo sample mean, rather than only the marginal covariance of a single draw.

    Parameters:
    chainarray-like, shape (n_samples, n_parameters)

    Mean-centered chain values. The caller must subtract the column means. mcse_multi performs this centering before calling this function.

    bint

    Lag-window bandwidth. Positive lags below b are included.

    method{‘bartlett’, ‘tukey’}

    Lag-window weighting rule. The default is ‘bartlett’.

    Returns:
    covariancenumpy.ndarray

    Spectral covariance estimate, with one row and column per parameter. Divide by n to estimate the covariance of the sample mean. Standard errors follow from sqrt(diag(covariance)/n).

    Notes

    For a centered chain, Gamma_k = chain[:-k].T @ chain[k:] / n. The estimator adds Gamma_0 once and, for each included positive lag, adds the window weight times Gamma_k + Gamma_k.T. In an independent chain, the positive-lag terms approach zero and spectral covariance approaches marginal covariance. Serial correlation can make those two covariance matrices quite different.
